newsitem.title: USA: Miami firm says seeks FBI probe of forged letter.
newsitem.headline: Miami firm says seeks FBI probe of forged letter.

text.p: The president of a Miami bond firm said he had asked the FBI to investigate a letter purportedly written under his signature, asking Dade County to dismiss another bond firm because of alleged wrongdoing.
The letter was dated Nov 27 and appeared to have been written by Leopoldo Guzman, on letterhead stationary for his firm, Guzman & Co.
"It's a fake. It's not our letter," Guzman told Reuters. "I am dumbfounded. It looks like they took a hell of a long time to imitate my signature."
He said the firm's attorney had asked the FBI office in Miami to investigate.
FBI spokesman Paul Miller said he could not immediately confirm that a complaint had been filed or what laws may apply.
"We don't normally acknowledge whether somebody makes a complaint or not. I'm not sure what our jurisdiction would be," Miller said. "It sounds like something we don't normally get complaints about."
Miller said a forged letter "sounds more like a postal inspection" matter, or possibly something the would fall under jurisdiction of the U.S. Attorney or the civil tort system.
The letter was addressed to Dade County Commissioner Jimmy Morales, chairman of the county budget, finance and public trust funds committee, which oversees bond county bond issues.

It accused another firm that has done bond work for the county of violating a Municipal Securities Rulmaking Board rule regarding distribution of fees. The letter said the firm should be removed from Dade County deals "to ensure the lowest prices for Dade County bond offerings" until the violations have been resolved.

Morales' chief of staff, Chip Iglesias, said the commissioner had not directly received the letter by fax but that "someone from the finance department" had, and gave Morales' staff a photocopy late Monday.
Iglesias said he did not know what, if anything, the county planned to do.
Officials for the firm accused in the letter said they were unaware of its existance until questioned by Reuters.
Guzman said he had no idea who would want to forge his signature or why. "This is not a nice business," he said.
